name: SBIR/STTR, DIU, xTech, AFWERX pattern analysis and proto-purgatory
summary: Across SBIR/STTR, DIU, xTech and AFWERX channels, C4ISR software themes are funded repeatedly, but the official data needed to prove transition is missing: GAO found in 2013 (GAO-14-96) and again in September 2025 (GAO-25-107942) that DoD cannot comprehensively measure SBIR transition outcomes, so 'proto-purgatory' must be inferred from proxies. DIU is the one channel that publishes a transition metric (51% of completed prototypes transitioned to production for FY2016-2023 per GAO-25-106856; DIU reported 13 more transitions in FY2024 and a 56% cumulative rate), but 'transition' means any production contract or program adoption, not scaled fielding. 2025-2026 evidence shows the fastest-moving demand signals in logistics C2 (DIU Joint Sustainment Decision Tool: launched Aug 2025, awards to Air Space Intelligence and Watchtower Labs Jan 2026, Gallatin AI for USAREUR-AF Jul 2026), AI-assisted planning (Thunderforge/Scale AI, Mar 2025), DDIL data integrity and zero-trust data tagging (NAVWAR open topic; XRDefense $4.75M AF Phase III), DevSecOps/continuous ATO (Rise8 PY2025 STRATFI) and GPS-denied edge autonomy (Tycho.AI $2M TACFI, May 2026; Compound Eye $13.3M Army SBIR CATALYST, Jul 2025). Track fusion and ISR PED show the opposite pattern: Navy topics on track-to-track fusion recur from 2011 (N111-016) through 2023 (N231-019) and 2025 (N252-089) with narrow Phase IIIs tied to classified combat-system integration, i.e. institutional barrier (B) more than open commercial demand. Big-ticket C2 programs (Army NGC2 prototype OTAs in 2025) went to teams led by well-capitalized firms, and the SBIR statutory lapse on 30 Sept 2025 plus the Oct-Nov 2025 shutdown put SBIR contracts on hold, with reauthorization/reform moving through Congress in 2026. Record private funding ($49.1B raised by defense-tech startups in 2025) is not military demand; production-bridge mechanisms (STRATFI/TACFI, Army CATALYST, APFIT, DIU CSO follow-ons) exist but are competitive and require government-customer sponsorship and matching money. For a two-founder team with $250k, SBIR ownership rules (>50% U.S. citizen/permanent-resident ownership) and matching-fund requirements are gating constraints that need specialist legal review.

findings.title: DIU reports a ~51-56% prototype-to-production transition rate, the only published transition metric among the innovation channels
findings.detail: GAO-25-106856 (Feb 2025) states DIU made 450 prototype awards FY2016-FY2023 and that 51% of completed prototypes transitioned to production; DIU leadership testimony (HASC, 2025) reported 13 additional transitions in FY2024 and a cumulative 56% rate. GAO nonetheless found DIU lacks performance goals to assess progress. 'Transition' in DIU usage includes any follow-on production contract or program adoption, not necessarily scaled fielding.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DIU reported that 51 percent of completed prototypes transitioned to production (GAO summary of DIU data, FY2016-2023, 450 awards).
findings.source_title: GAO-25-106856, Defense Innovation Unit: Actions Needed to Assess Progress and Further Enhance Collaboration
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: DIU is the channel with the best documented odds of a follow-on; roughly half of completed prototypes get some production follow-on, but the definition is loose and the base is dominated by hardware and autonomy projects.

findings.title: DIU's CSO + OT model has produced 500+ prototype awards and is being scaled across DoD as the default commercial on-ramp
findings.detail: DIU pioneered the Commercial Solutions Opening process in 2016; its own software-acquisition-reform page states DIU has conducted more than 500 CSO-OT awards over eight years and (as of March 2025) plans to scale CSO plus OT authority across a broader range of DoD users. This matters because CSO awards do not require small-business status and carry no SBIR ownership rules.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DIU has conducted more than 500 CSO-OT awards over the past eight years; accelerating commercial technology is core to DIU's mission with plans to scale the CSO process combined with OT authority across a broader range of DoD users.
findings.source_title: DIU: Advancing DoD operational capabilities with software acquisition reform
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: A CSO/OT path avoids SBIR ownership constraints relevant to a non-U.S.-person co-founder, but FOCI/ITAR still apply and must be reviewed by counsel.

findings.title: GAO has repeatedly found DoD cannot comprehensively measure SBIR transition outcomes (2013, 2014, 2025)
findings.detail: GAO-14-96 (Dec 2013) and GAO-14-748T (Jul 2014) concluded DoD's SBIR program developed some technologies that transitioned to acquisition programs or fielded systems but that the extent is unknown because comprehensive, reliable transition data are not collected. GAO-25-107942 (Sep 2025) again found award data quality (including Phase I-to-II and commercialization outcomes) needs clearer guidance to measure outcomes. Consequently, any 'proto-purgatory' quantification must rely on proxies (Phase III announcements, STRATFI/CATALYST/APFIT awards, DIU transitions, M&A).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DOD's SBIR program has developed some technologies that successfully transitioned... but the extent of transition is unknown because comprehensive and reliable transition data are not collected.
findings.source_title: GAO-14-748T and GAO-25-107942 (Small Business Research Programs: Clearer Guidance Could Improve Award Data to More Effectively Measure Outcomes)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Founders should not trust program-level transition claims; diligence must be per-company (named Phase III/production contracts, repeat orders).

findings.title: AFWERX STRATFI/TACFI is the Air Force's formal bridge from Phase II to production: $3-15M (STRATFI) and $375K-2M (TACFI), Phase II within two years, matching funds required; PY26.1 cycle opened in 2025
findings.detail: AFVentures administers STRATFI and TACFI as sequential SBIR Phase II bridge awards. Eligibility is limited to successful Phase II projects within two years of award, and both require matching funds from a government customer and/or private investors (exact ratios are in the PY26.1 Notice of Opportunity, AFRL-2025-3392, which the egress proxy blocked this session). The 2024 cycle NoO was published in 2023 and a PY26.1 NoO was posted in 2025, showing the mechanism continued through the 2025 SBIR authorization lapse.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: STRATFI awards range from $3 million to $15 million; TACFI awards range from $375,000 to $2 million. STRATFI/TACFI eligibility is limited to successful Phase II projects within 2 years of award.
findings.source_title: AFWERX Sequential Opportunities (STRATFI/TACFI) and PY26.1 STRATFI Notice of Opportunity
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: A STRATFI requires an Air Force customer willing to commit funds plus private match; with $250k of capital the team would need outside investors to satisfy the match, which is the real gate.

findings.title: Rise8 selected for PY2025 STRATFI to enable rapid continuous delivery of mission-critical applications (DevSecOps/ATO theme graduates to bridge funding)
findings.detail: AFWERX and SpaceWERX selected Rise8 for a Program Year 2025 STRATFI under the U.S. Air Force SBIR program (announced 19 Mar 2025). Rise8 is a continuous-delivery/ATO-pipeline vendor rather than a C2 application vendor, which illustrates that the DAF is bridge-funding the delivery infrastructure for C2 software rather than only the apps themselves.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: AFWERX and SpaceWERX Select Rise8 for Program Year 2025 STRATFI under U.S. Air Force SBIR to Enable Rapid, Continuous Delivery of Mission-Critical Applications.
findings.source_title: GlobeNewswire press release (Rise8)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: DevSecOps/continuous-ATO is a theme where SBIR money has demonstrably converted to bridge funding; it is also crowded (Rise8, Raft, Defense Unicorns, Second Front - the latter three RECALL, not re-verified).

findings.title: Tycho.AI won an 18-month $2M AFRL TACFI (May 2026) for GPS-denied, comms-contested maritime autonomy - edge AI/PNT-denied autonomy is still being bridge-funded in 2026
findings.detail: Tycho.AI announced a $2 million TACFI from AFRL for autonomy software and mission-optimized compute for unmanned systems operating without persistent connectivity or remote control. TACFI is the ceiling-size ($2M) award, indicating a successful Phase II but not yet a production program.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Tycho.AI Secures $2M AFRL TACFI Contract to Advance Maritime Autonomy in GPS-Denied Environments... edge-executable AI enabling intelligent navigation and operation without remote control or persistent connectivity.
findings.source_title: GlobeNewswire press release (Tycho.AI)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Confirms continuing demand for DDIL-tolerant edge autonomy, but the award is a bridge, not production; company marketing is not proof the product works.

findings.title: Intellisense Systems' STRATFI (May 2024) was explicitly to 'finalize transition' of its weather observation system - STRATFI is used as a named transition instrument, mostly for hardware/sensor products
findings.detail: Intellisense received an AFWERX STRATFI to finalize transition of the Integrated Weather Observation System (IWOS). Together with OrbitFab's $12M STRATFI (in-space refueling), the visible STRATFI cohort skews toward hardware and space products; C2/data-software STRATFIs found this session were Rise8 (DevSecOps) and, by recall, Second Front (Game Warden). Public evidence on a full PY2025/PY2026 STRATFI list is insufficient (AFWERX and SpaceWERX pages blocked).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Intellisense Systems awarded USAF STRATFI contract to finalize transition of the IWOS.
findings.source_title: Intellisense Systems press release
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Pure-software C2 startups are under-represented among named STRATFI winners relative to sensors/hardware; the exception is DevSecOps infrastructure.

findings.title: DIU Thunderforge: prototype OT to Scale AI (Mar 2025) to integrate commercial AI into operational and theater-level planning - a C2 decision-support prototype, not a production program
findings.detail: DIU announced Thunderforge, awarding a prototype contract to Scale AI to integrate AI agents into military planning workflows at combatant commands (INDOPACOM and EUCOM per DIU; RECALL for the specific commands). Partners reportedly include Anduril and Microsoft (RECALL, not re-verified). This is prototype-stage; no production transition is documented as of this sweep.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DIU's Thunderforge project to integrate commercial AI-powered decision making... awarded a prototype contract to Scale AI.
findings.source_title: DIU: Thunderforge project to integrate commercial AI-powered decision making
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: The AI-for-planning lane at the theater level is already occupied by a well-capitalized incumbent team; a student startup would be a subcontractor or niche data/tool provider at best.

findings.title: Logistics C2 shows the fastest 2025-2026 DIU cadence: JSDT launched Aug 2025, prototype OTs to Air Space Intelligence and Watchtower Labs Jan 2026, Gallatin AI added for USAREUR-AF Jul 2026
findings.detail: DIU's Joint Sustainment Decision Tool (JSDT) aims to use commercial AI to anticipate logistics requirements and manage distribution weeks in advance. Two prototype contracts went to ASI and Watchtower Labs in January 2026 (about five months after launch); a further award to Gallatin AI to bring AI-driven sustainment planning to U.S. Army Europe and Africa was announced 15 Jul 2026. Multiple awards to relatively young companies indicate an open, actively funded lane.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The JSDT team awarded two prototype contracts to Air Space Intelligence (ASI) and Watchtower Labs, Inc. in January 2026... Launched in August 2025, JSDT aims to leverage advanced commercial AI tools to anticipate logistics requirements and proactively manage distribution weeks in advance.
findings.source_title: DIU: Two contracts awarded to modernize decision making for DoW's joint logistics; Gallatin AI press release (PR Newswire)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Logistics/sustainment C2 is a demand lane where new entrants won DIU prototypes in 2026; it is less crowded than kinetic C2 and has lower classification friction, but transition to a program of record is not yet shown.

findings.title: DIU Common Operational Database (COD) with Project Overmatch/NAVWAR: DDIL-resilient database for unmanned systems, started mid-2023, DIU claims deployment of commercial AI solutions
findings.detail: In mid-2023 DIU partnered with Project Overmatch and NAVWAR to source commercial solutions for a Common Operational Database enabling unmanned systems to operate in DDIL environments. A later DIU release is titled 'DoD Successfully Deploys Commercial AI Solutions for COD Project'. Vendor names and deployment scale were not captured in this session (DIU pages blocked to fetch).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DIU partnered with Project Overmatch and the Naval Information Warfare Systems Command to identify state-of-the-art commercial solutions for a Common Operational Database to allow unmanned systems to operate effectively in DDIL environments.
findings.source_title: DIU: Department of Defense successfully deploys commercial AI solutions for COD project
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: DDIL data synchronization for unmanned fleets is a validated Navy need with a DIU deployment claim; a startup entering now competes against vendors already integrated into Overmatch.

findings.title: A 2025 DIU solicitation seeks DDIL-tolerant targeting for small dispersed strike teams with minimal reliance on external data links
findings.detail: A DIU submission opportunity (surfaced alongside Project G.I., PROJ00598, presented with NSIN in Dec 2025) asks for commercial solutions that speed the targeting cycle for small, dispersed target-strike teams under DDIL conditions so they can independently detect, identify and engage high-value targets. Exact project attribution is uncertain because the DIU page could not be fetched.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The DoD seeks commercial solutions to enhance the targeting-cycle speed for small, dispersed target-strike teams operating under DDIL conditions... with minimal reliance on external data links.
findings.source_title: DIU Submission Opportunity - Project G.I. (PROJ00598) / NSIN event page
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Edge, disconnected targeting workflows remain an open DIU ask in late 2025; this is the clearest 'persistent unmet demand' signal for DDIL software, though it favors teams with sensor/EO-IR and fires-integration expertise.

findings.title: NAVWAR open SBIR topic 'Data Integrity and Control in DDIL Environments' ties zero-trust data formats (ZTDF/ICDF) to DDIL operation - topic wording that recurs across services
findings.detail: The Navy topic asks for data protected as an object independent of network, application or database, using formats such as Intelligence Community Data Format (ICDF) and Zero Trust Data Format (ZTDF), functioning in disrupted, disconnected, intermittent and low-bandwidth conditions and recovering gracefully when connectivity returns. This wording (object-level data control + DDIL) is the same problem framing as data-fabric and NGC2 'data-centric' language.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Proposed solutions must protect data independent of networks, applications, or database technologies, function in disrupted, disconnected, intermittent and low-bandwidth (DDIL) situations, and recover gracefully once connectivity is restored to normal.
findings.source_title: SBIR.gov topic (NAVWAR open topic: Data Integrity and Control in DDIL Environments)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Zero-trust data tagging that survives DDIL is a well-specified, software-only problem where an SBIR Phase I/II is realistic for a small engineering team; the standards (ZTDF/TDF) are open.

findings.title: XRDefense LLC received a $4.75M Air Force SBIR Phase III for zero-trust data fabric - a visible but small Phase III in the data-fabric theme
findings.detail: A contract-award aggregator reports a $4,750,000 Air Force SBIR Phase III award to XRDefense LLC for zero trust data fabric work. The award date was not captured; the amount is a Phase III contract value, not revenue recognized. It shows that data-fabric SBIR work does convert to Phase III, but at single-digit-million scale.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Contract Award: $5M Air Force SBIR Phase III Zero Trust Data Fabric (XRDefense LLC, $4,750,000).
findings.source_title: OrangeSlices AI contract award note
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Benchmark for what a 'graduation' looks like in this theme: a ~$5M Phase III, which sustains a small firm but is not a scaled program of record.

findings.title: Navy FY26 Release 3 SBIR/STTR topics include zero-trust data for combat systems and sensor management; Navy 25.2 topic N252-089 asks for a 'Virtual Agent for Data Fusion and Understanding'
findings.detail: ExecutiveGov reports the Navy's FY26 Release 3 topics cover satellite imagery, zero-trust data for combat systems and sensor management. The Navy 25.2 cycle (pre-release 2 Apr 2025, open 23 Apr, close 21 May 2025) included N252-089, a virtual agent for data fusion whose Phase III is defined as integration into operational platforms and future combat systems. Topic wording 'data fusion and understanding', 'sensor management', 'zero trust data' recurs.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Navy FY26 Release 3 SBIR and STTR topics covering satellite imagery, zero trust data for combat systems and sensor management.
findings.source_title: ExecutiveGov: Navy discloses topics for SBIR-STTR FY26 Release 3 solicitation; navysbir.com N252-089
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Navy continues to buy fusion/PED research via SBIR every cycle, but Phase III is defined as combat-system integration, which requires prime cooperation and clearances.

findings.title: Army SBIR topic 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' funds a DDIL tactical-network simulation environment for NGC2 - SBIR is being used to build test infrastructure around NGC2 rather than NGC2 itself
findings.detail: The Army SBIR topic's objective is a realistic modeling-and-simulation environment using generative AI for NGC2, reflecting a DDIL tactical network with multiple real-time data access and delivery demands. This indicates the Army uses SBIR to fill supporting gaps (test/M&S) while the core NGC2 prototype is awarded via CSO/OT to large vendor teams.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Create a realistic modeling and simulation environment using Generative AI for NGC2... reflecting a realistic tactical network (DDIL environment) with multiple data access and delivery demands in real time.
findings.source_title: Army SBIR|STTR Program: Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network topic
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Adjacent tooling for NGC2 (network emulation, data-load simulation, test harnesses) is an SBIR-accessible niche for a small software team that cannot compete for the NGC2 prime prototype.

findings.title: Army NGC2 prototype OTAs (2025) were competed via CSO and awarded to vendor teams for 4th ID, then 25th ID/III Corps - prototypes led by well-capitalized firms, not SBIR graduates
findings.detail: Army.mil announced an NGC2 prototype award (article 287180, mid-2025) and an 'additional competitive award' (article 288233) via a Commercial Solutions Opening, with further OTAs planned in FY2025 for 25th Infantry Division and III Corps. By recall (not re-verified this session), the first award went to an Anduril-led team and the second to a Lockheed Martin-led team. These are prototype OTAs; NGC2 is not yet a production program of record.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The Army is executing a competition for additional vendors and vendor teams through a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), with additional OTA(s) expected to be awarded later in Fiscal Year 2025 for NGC2 prototyping with other units, including the 25th Infantry Division and III Corps Headquarters.
findings.source_title: Army.mil: Army announces additional competitive award for NGC2 prototyping efforts
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: The flagship Army C2 lane is a team sport led by large integrators; a startup's realistic entry is as a specialty app or data-service supplier inside a team, not as a lead.

findings.title: Army SBIR CATALYST: Compound Eye secured $13.3M in full CATALYST funding (Jul 2025) for VIDAS-SLAM - the Army's dedicated Phase II-to-III bridge is being used for GPS-denied navigation software
findings.detail: Compound Eye (visual inertial SLAM for GPS-denied navigation) received an additional $13.3M under the Army SBIR CATALYST program in July 2025. CATALYST pools Army SBIR and program-office funds to move Phase II technologies toward Phase III; award sizes of this magnitude exceed a standard Phase II by roughly an order of magnitude.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: In July 2025, Compound Eye secured full SBIR CATALYST funding - an additional $13.3 million to accelerate VIDAS-SLAM development.
findings.source_title: Akela Consultants: Army SBIR Program overview (citing Compound Eye CATALYST award)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: PNT-denied navigation software is one of the few C4ISR-adjacent software themes with a documented eight-figure Army bridge award to a venture-backed startup.

findings.title: xTechOverwatch (launched 2 Apr 2025): $1M cash prizes and up to $40M in follow-on SBIR awards for autonomy/AI/sensor small businesses; 40 finalists, up to 20 winners at the Oct 2025 Army summit
findings.detail: The Army xTech program with Army Futures Command selected 40 finalists ($15,000 each) to demonstrate at the October 2025 Army Unmanned Systems/HMI Summit, with up to 20 winners ($20,000 each) and an xTechOverwatch SBIR open topic enabling follow-on awards totaling up to $40M. xTech prize competitions function as an on-ramp to Army SBIR Phase I/II rather than to production.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: xTech Overwatch advances Army's autonomous capabilities with $1M in cash prizes and $40M in follow-on awards.
findings.source_title: Army SBIR|STTR Program announcement; xtech.army.mil finalists announcement
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: xTech is the cheapest, fastest Army on-ramp for a two-person team (no prior Phase I needed), but prize money is small and the $40M follow-on pool is split across many winners.

findings.title: Navy track-fusion topics recur across 14+ years (N111-016 in 2011, N231-019 in 2023, N252-089 in 2025) with Phase III notices still being issued for the 2011 topic - a perpetual-prototyping signature
findings.detail: A sam.gov notice exists for a Phase III under topic N111-016 'Optimizing Track-to-Track Data Fusion for Variable Cases' (2011 topic), while N231-019 'Big Data Analytics: Real-Time Data Mining and Track Fusion of National and Tactical Data' (2023) and N252-089 (2025) re-pose similar fusion problems. Recurrence of near-identical topic wording over more than a decade, combined with Phase IIIs scoped to 'refine, test and integrate' into combat systems, indicates the barrier is integration into classified programs of record, not absence of algorithms.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: SBIR Phase III Topic N111-016 Optimizing Track-to-Track Data Fusion (sam.gov); N231-019 Phase III: refine the design, test, and integrate the architecture and algorithms.
findings.source_title: sam.gov Phase III notice for N111-016; navysbir.com N231-019
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Track fusion is a mature, incumbent-heavy SBIR niche (Toyon, Numerica, Metron, SSCI - RECALL) where new entrants face both algorithmic incumbents and classified integration gates; verdict B (institutional barrier).

findings.title: ISR PED example: Wilson Eagle/Ausgar/Jove Sciences plan Phase III transition of ACOR-N and Pattern-of-Life Processor into the C2X program at SECRET and TS/SCI levels - classification is the transition gate
findings.detail: An sbir.gov award record describes the Advanced Correlator-Navy (ACOR-N) and Pattern Of Life Processor (POLP) developed by a small-business team for transition to the Command and Control Experimentation (C2X) program under a Phase III follow-on, noting C2X capability at SECRET with initial TS/SCI development. Transition therefore depends on cleared facilities and personnel, which student founders (one non-U.S. person) would not have.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: ...for transition to the Command and Control Experimentation (C2X) program during a Phase III follow-on contract, with C2X having a well-developed tested capability at the SECRET level and initial development at the TS/SCI level.
findings.source_title: SBIR.gov award record 8672
findings.pub_date: Public evidence insufficient (award year not captured).
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: ISR PED transitions run through classified enclaves; without a facility clearance and cleared U.S.-person staff the theme is effectively closed to this founding team in the near term (legal/FSO review required).

findings.title: SBIR/STTR authority lapsed 30 Sep 2025 and the Oct-Nov 2025 shutdown put SBIR contracts on hold; the Senate passed a reauthorization through 2031 with major reforms on 25 Feb 2026 and the program is being 'revamped for modern warfare'
findings.detail: Breaking Defense (Oct 2025) reported the small-business fund used by DoD 'teeters on the edge' amid a fight over 'SBIR mills'; Air & Space Forces Magazine reported SBIR contracts on hold during the shutdown faced long-term risk; Defense News (29 Sep 2025) reported small defense firms warning of industrial-base harm. The Senate unanimously passed the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act on 25 Feb 2026 (reauthorization through 2031 with structural reforms); DefenseScoop (29 Apr 2026) described the program being revamped. Final enactment status and the reform details were not verified this session.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Pentagon's small business innovation fund in jeopardy (Breaking Defense, Oct 2025); The Senate unanimously passed the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act on February 25, 2026, reauthorizing SBIR and STTR through 2031.
findings.source_title: Breaking Defense; Air & Space Forces Magazine; DefenseScoop ('America's seed fund' is being revamped for modern warfare)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: SBIR is a politically volatile funding rail; a plan that depends on Phase I/II cash-flow timing in 2026-2027 must budget for lapses and reform-driven rule changes (e.g., caps on repeat awardees).

findings.title: Army is reorienting SBIR toward integrated capabilities ('the whole vs. the parts'), consistent with CATALYST and NGC2 team-based buying
findings.detail: Federal News Network (May 2026) reports the Army moving SBIR to focus on whole capabilities rather than component technologies. Combined with CATALYST pooling and the NGC2 CSO structure, this suggests component-level C2 software SBIRs will increasingly need to plug into named integrated efforts to be funded.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Army moving SBIR to focus on the whole vs. the parts.
findings.source_title: Federal News Network, Ask the CIO
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: A narrow point solution is less fundable in the Army channel than before; positioning as a module of a named capability (NGC2 data layer, HMI formation) improves odds.

findings.title: APFIT (Accelerate Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies) has surpassed $1B in cumulative awards - a production bridge that complements SBIR Phase III and DIU follow-ons
findings.detail: A Tier-4 grant-advisory blog reports the Pentagon crossed $1 billion in cumulative APFIT awards; APFIT funds procurement of already-prototyped small-business/non-traditional technologies. Program-level totals were not verified against comptroller documents this session. APFIT funding is procurement money, but individual awards are typically single-digit to low-double-digit millions and are announced per project.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The Pentagon just crossed $1 billion in APFIT awards.
findings.source_title: Granted AI blog: Pentagon APFIT billion / SBIR return
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: APFIT is a real but competitive procurement bridge; to date it has favored hardware and platforms (RECALL), so software C2 startups should not plan around it.

findings.title: Defense-tech startups raised a record $49.1B in 2025 (nearly double 2024) and 107+ venture rounds by mid-2026, while continuing resolutions meant 'no new starts' - funding is not demand
findings.detail: Defense News (20 Jan 2026) reports defense-tech startups raised $49.1B in 2025 vs $27.2B in 2024 (equity funding $17.9B); Crunchbase counts 107 defense-tech venture rounds in 2026 to date. Defense One (Nov 2025) notes that continuing resolutions prevent new starts, so contracts startups projected for Q1 2026 might not occur. Investor interest is therefore running ahead of obligated military demand.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Defense tech startups raised $49.1 billion in 2025, nearly doubling from $27.2 billion in 2024... continuing resolutions mean no new starts, so contracts they had projected starting in Q1 of 2026 might not happen.
findings.source_title: Defense News: Defense tech startups had their best funding year ever in 2025; Defense One: Defense tech companies will weather the shutdown
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Capital is abundant for defense software, which raises the competitive bar for a $250k team; the scarce resource is a government customer with obligated funds.

findings.title: M&A is the dominant visible 'graduation' for SBIR-heritage C4ISR firms in 2025-2026: Forterra acquired goTenna (tactical mesh networking); Firefly acquired SciTec ($855M); CACI acquired ARKA ($2.6B); Motorola acquired D-Fend ($1.5B)
findings.detail: Reporting on 2025-2026 defense M&A lists Forterra's purchase of goTenna (mesh-networking startup with Army SBIR/Phase III heritage - heritage is RECALL, not re-verified), Firefly Aerospace's $855M acquisition of SciTec (missile-warning/tracking software with heavy SBIR heritage - RECALL) and CACI's $2.6B ARKA purchase. These show that tactical networking and sensor-processing software firms exit via acquisition more often than via becoming a program-of-record prime.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Forterra purchased GoTenna, a mesh networking startup... Firefly Aerospace's $855 million acquisition of SciTec... CACI International's $2.6 billion acquisition of ARKA Group.
findings.source_title: Defense News 2026 outlook / White & Case M&A Explorer: Boots off the ground
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: For tactical-networking and fusion software, the realistic upside case is acquisition by a prime or scaled startup, not independent scale; this shapes what to build (integratable modules).

findings.title: Rebellion Defense is the canonical 'raised big, faded' C2-software case: ~40% workforce cut in May 2023 after a >$1B valuation in 2021
findings.detail: Layoffs.fyi records Rebellion Defense laying off as much as 40% of staff in May 2023 with layoff history since 2020. By recall (not re-verified this session), Rebellion raised a $150M Series B in 2021 at a >$1B valuation for AI-enabled mission software, cycled through CEOs, and narrowed to cyber/defensive products. No 2025-2026 shutdown was found; the company is smaller and less visible rather than closed.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Rebellion Defense laid off as much as 40% of its workforce (May 2023).
findings.source_title: Layoffs.fyi: Rebellion Defense
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Lesson: venture scale without a program of record or repeat orders leads to contraction; the C2 'AI mission software' pitch alone did not convert to durable revenue.

findings.title: Radiant Logic selected to create the Naval Identity Service (Nov 2022) - commercial ICAM/zero-trust software reaching enterprise adoption via a non-SBIR path
findings.detail: The Department of the Navy selected Radiant Logic (a commercial identity-data vendor) for the Naval Identity Service, an enterprise zero-trust ICAM foundation. This is a production enterprise selection rather than a prototype, showing zero-trust identity/data control has a buyer with budget, although the winner was an established commercial firm rather than an SBIR startup.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The Department of Navy selects Radiant Logic to create Naval Identity Service.
findings.source_title: Business Wire press release
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Zero trust has real production budgets, but enterprise ICAM is taken by established vendors; the open edge is tactical/DDIL data tagging (see F12).

findings.title: Recurring SBIR specialist firms dominate C2 decision-support, fusion and PED topics (Toyon, Numerica, Charles River Analytics, Aptima, SoarTech, Stottler Henke, Perceptronics, Metron, Scientific Systems) - the 'SBIR mill' pattern targeted by 2025-2026 reform
findings.detail: RECALL - not re-verified this session: these firms appear repeatedly as Phase I/II awardees on Navy/Air Force/Army topics for track fusion, sensor management, decision aids and PED tools across 2019-2025, with Phase IIIs typically as subcontracts to primes or lab follow-ons. The 2025 reauthorization fight explicitly targeted repeat awardees ('SBIR mills'), per Breaking Defense (Oct 2025).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: 'Clean those bastards out': small business fund used by DoD teeters on the edge (Breaking Defense headline on the SBIR-mill dispute).
findings.source_title: Breaking Defense: Pentagon's small business innovation fund in jeopardy
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Repeat awardees crowd the fusion/decision-aid topic space; reform-era caps on repeat awardees could open room for new entrants, but Phase III access still runs through primes and labs.

findings.title: DevSecOps/ATO 'graduations' (Second Front Game Warden, Rise8, Raft, Defense Unicorns) show software-delivery infrastructure is the clearest SBIR-to-production lane in C4ISR software
findings.detail: RECALL - not re-verified this session except Rise8 (F5): Second Front Systems' Game Warden received AFWERX STRATFI funding and DoD authorizations enabling commercial apps to be hosted at IL5/IL6; Raft and Defense Unicorns grew from SBIR/Platform One work to multi-million Air Force and Space Force software contracts. The common thread is selling the path-to-ATO rather than a C2 application, and lining up a specific customer (Platform One, Kessel Run, Space Force) before the bridge award.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Rise8 STRATFI for rapid, continuous delivery of mission-critical applications (verified); Game Warden/Raft/Defense Unicorns transitions are recall.
findings.source_title: Rise8 STRATFI announcement (verified) plus recall of company press releases
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Verdict A (persistent demand with real graduations) but crowded and consolidating; a new entrant needs a differentiated wedge (e.g., DDIL/edge deployment of ATO'd apps).

findings.title: Founder-eligibility constraints: SBIR/STTR requires a U.S. small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents; STRATFI/TACFI require matching funds; DIU CSO has no small-business rule but FOCI/ITAR/export controls apply
findings.detail: Under SBA SBIR/STTR policy directives (stable rule, RECALL), the applicant must be a for-profit U.S. small business more than 50% directly owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent resident aliens (or by other qualifying small businesses/VC-backed structures with agency election), with work performed in the U.S. A team where one founder is a non-U.S. person and one is a German national pending permanent residency would need to structure ownership carefully; ITAR/EAR deemed-export rules and FOCI mitigation for any cleared work require specialist legal review. STRATFI/TACFI matching requirements (government and private match) are set out in the AFWERX Notice of Opportunity (blocked this session).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: STRATFI/TACFI eligibility is limited to successful Phase II projects within 2 years of award (AFWERX FAQ); ownership rule per SBA policy directive (recall).
findings.source_title: AFWERX STRATFI/TACFI eligibility FAQ; Army SBIR eligibility page
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: This is a gating item: without a compliant ownership structure the SBIR/STRATFI/CATALYST rails are unavailable, leaving DIU CSO, prime subcontracting and allied markets; do not proceed without immigration/export-control counsel.

findings.title: Coalition interoperability/Mission Partner Environment and spectrum-awareness software: no SBIR/DIU/AFWERX awards or topics surfaced this session
findings.detail: Twelve targeted searches did not surface MPE/coalition-interop or spectrum-awareness SBIR, DIU or STRATFI awards for 2024-2026. By recall (LOW confidence), MPE is procured via DISA/Joint Staff J6 enterprise vehicles rather than SBIR, and spectrum-awareness startups (e.g., Distributed Spectrum, CX2) have relied on venture funding plus AFWERX/Army SBIR Phase I/II rather than documented production transitions. Public evidence insufficient.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Public evidence insufficient.
findings.source_title: Public evidence insufficient.
findings.label: HYPOTHESIS
findings.startup_relevance: Absence of evidence is not opportunity; these themes need a dedicated sweep of DISA, JS J6, and Army EW program offices rather than SBIR databases.

findings.title: Baseline: DIU's FY2022 record of 17 transitions and its FY2024 count of 13 imply low double-digit transitions per year across all technology areas, i.e. only a handful per year in C2/software
findings.detail: Breaking Defense (Jan 2023) reported DIU transitioned 17 technologies in FY2022, a record; the FY2024 figure of 13 (from DIU testimony) suggests the annual count has plateaued. Given DIU's portfolio mix (autonomy, space, energy, cyber, AI, human systems), the number of C2/data-software transitions per year is likely in the low single digits (INFERENCE).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: From prototypes to operations: in record-breaking year, DIU transitioned 17 new tech.
findings.source_title: Breaking Defense
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Even the best-performing channel produces roughly a dozen transitions a year across DoD; a startup's plan should assume a multi-year, low-probability path and diversify customers.

themes.verdict: A/B mixed: the problem recurs (A) but Phase IIIs are small and the big money flows through integrated programs (B).

founder_analysis.sbir_eligibility: SBIR/STTR requires a U.S. for-profit small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (RECALL of SBA policy directive; stable rule). An Indonesian founder who is not a U.S. person and a German founder pending permanent residency create an ownership-structure question that must be resolved with counsel before relying on SBIR, STRATFI/TACFI or CATALYST.
founder_analysis.diu_cso_path: DIU CSO/OT has no small-business ownership test, making it the most accessible rail, but export controls (ITAR/EAR deemed exports to a non-U.S.-person co-founder), FOCI mitigation for any cleared work, and CMMC apply; specialist legal review required.
founder_analysis.capital_fit: $250k covers a Phase I ($150-300k typical, RECALL) or an xTech entry but not a STRATFI private match; the team would need outside investors or a government sponsor before bridge funding is realistic.
founder_analysis.theme_fit: Best-fit lanes given constraints: zero-trust/DDIL data tagging (open standards, software-only, recurring topics), logistics C2 (DIU-led, unclassified, new entrants winning), NGC2-adjacent test/M&S tooling. Poor-fit lanes: ISR PED and track fusion (classified integration), theater-level AI planning (occupied), tactical transport (hardware/incumbents).

saturation_statement: Not saturated. Twelve searches and two blocked fetches established program mechanics, 2025-2026 marquee awards (Rise8 STRATFI, Tycho.AI TACFI, Compound Eye CATALYST, DIU JSDT and Thunderforge, NGC2 OTAs), GAO's finding that transition data are inadequate, and the SBIR lapse/reauthorization timeline.
